messages.author: 65ee6740f5492ac2
messages.subject: cleanGeno for maps with 3 genotypes
parts:
Hello, 

To remove doublecrossover events with only single markers, Karl wrote the function cleanGeno(). It has a limitation to be only working for maps based on 2 genotypes, A or B. 

I just tested it on a F2 population (A, H, B) and it seems to work fine as well at least using maxmark = 1.  

Could you tell me what could go wrong applying your function to 3 genotype data?

Thank you, 
Michel

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] cleanGeno for maps with 3 genotypes
parts:
The cleanGeno() function looks for tight double crossovers, but in an intercross, these can be real, because there could be one on each chromosome; for example AB -> AA -> AB might be AAB|BAA.

karl

Hmm, i dont get the point. AB -> AA -> AB would still be highly unlikely if AA would only be supported by a single marker in between and should be removed.

I thought the method loacteXO looks for any changes in genotypes for a sequence of markers which are encoded as being 1 (AA) or 2 (BB) or 3 (if you have AA AB BB). So any change of genotype of marker length 1 is unlikely and gets removed by cleanGeno?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] cleanGeno for maps with 3 genotypes
parts:
In a backcross, having two crossovers right next to each other is highly unlikely due to crossover interference.
But in an intercross the two crossovers may have occurred on opposite chromosomes, and so would not be barred by crossover interference.

That was my thinking, anyway.

karl
